epilogue.collapse_breakdown: The unresolved breakdown ends the expedition. Trump said the tariffs would be paid overseas. The repair quote has spent the whole discussion looking directly at you.
epilogue.collapse_hunger: Hunger ends the expedition. Congress cut projected food-aid spending and called it savings. You cannot eat the forecast, although it now contains a very impressive number.
epilogue.collapse_vehicle: Vehicle condition ends the expedition. Trump gave defense a fiercer name. You could try the same with the van, but “unstoppable” would now be blocking traffic.
epilogue.collapse_weather: Weather ends the expedition. Sharpiegate demonstrated how to change a forecast with a pen. Nobody demonstrated how to drive across the correction.
epilogue.exposure: 中暑或冻伤，天气结束了政治的开始。
epilogue.generic: This account does not say how the journey ended. After the bombing-plan group chat, check the recipient list. The government may have sent the conclusion to a man who sells patio furniture.
epilogue.vehicle_failure_vehicle_destroyed: The van is destroyed. The journey ends with American travelers unable to travel. The tariff pitch promised to protect domestic industry; your contribution now appears to be scrap.
epilogue.exposure_cold: Cold exposure ends the journey. The political fundraiser’s dinner is kept warm under little silver lids. Apparently even a potato can obtain better representation.
epilogue.exposure_heat: Heat exposure ends the expedition. Politicians who oppose mandatory worker heat breaks make their case indoors. The thermostat has been allowed to regulate without a public hearing.
epilogue.boss_loss: The final vote goes against you. You brought evidence, testimony and an actual journey. The donor envelope brought none of these and gets invited to dinner.
epilogue.collapse: The journey ended before the hearing could be completed.
epilogue.sanity: You cannot keep going; your sanity is exhausted. Officials who put bombing plans in a group chat will continue lecturing everyone about judgment. Yours has at least recognized an emergency.
epilogue.victory: You win the final vote. A lobbyist asks which super PAC backed you. You show the laundry change. He looks underneath it for the billionaire.
epilogue.collapse_panic: Panic ends the expedition. Officials who misplaced bombing plans will continue explaining that everyone else is overreacting. You switch off the briefing; it is the first thing to stop escalating.
epilogue.collapse_disease: Illness ends the expedition. Congress wants work documented before more people can keep benefits. Your body has been doing nothing but fight. It has neglected to create a login.
epilogue.collapse_crossing: The crossing ends the expedition. In American politics, enormous sums move freely as independent speech. Your actual people have encountered a less accommodating barrier.
epilogue.incomplete: This journey is unfinished. In Washington, the donor dinner is still on the calendar. The chicken has secured an appointment; your case is still on the road.

headline.collapse_panic: Nothing to See, Too Much to Hear

beltway_briefing.name: The memory wash
beltway_briefing.desc: A roadside museum copying Trump’s Smithsonian history order has installed a “patriotic rinse.” Your crew is invited to test it with a public eviction account. The dryer returns a story about families discovering fresh air. One sock still contains a bailiff.
beltway_briefing.choice_0: Use your paper; document the rinse
beltway_briefing.log_0: You use some supplies tracing every altered line, head pounding. The original account survives. The dryer requests a gentler historical cycle.
beltway_briefing.choice_1: Let the rinse improve your account
beltway_briefing.log_1: The cleaned-up account is soothing and wrong. A resident points out that “voluntary camping” began when the locks changed.
beltway_briefing.log_2: You repeat the display’s version and get corrected. The resident brings a key. It fits the history considerably better than the caption.

classic_bridge_crews.name: Smaller government
classic_bridge_crews.desc: DOGE fired the park’s cleaners. The remaining ranger hasn’t had lunch. She offers your crew gloves beside overflowing bins. “Congratulations. You’re the smaller government.”
classic_bridge_crews.choice_0: Share some food and help clear the bins
classic_bridge_crews.log_0: You share lunch and haul bags until your back aches. She hands you a bin liner. “Uniform allowance.”
classic_bridge_crews.choice_1: Photograph the mess for your D.C. case
classic_bridge_crews.log_1: You photograph the overflowing bins. She points at the flies. “Only department still recruiting.”

deep_secure_line.name: The employed calendar
deep_secure_line.desc: A roadside benefits workshop previews Medicaid work checks due from 2027. Your crew is invited to inspect its calendar machine. It stamps every working day “prove it,” then adds a new day for proving it. The cleaner’s week has developed an extension.
deep_secure_line.choice_0: Check and save the rollout dates
deep_secure_line.log_0: You save the actual rollout dates and clear up the confusion. The cleaner removes the extra day. It still appears on the paperwork.
deep_secure_line.choice_1: Report that the federal rollout already happened
deep_secure_line.log_1: You repeat the premature claim and get corrected. The calendar machine has confused preparing for the deadline with surviving it.
deep_secure_line.choice_2: Use your paper; copy the rules
deep_secure_line.log_2: You use some supplies to copy the rules accurately. The volunteer puts the extra day in a folder. It no longer fits the week.

raw_milk.name: Uniformly absent
raw_milk.desc: At a park stop after DOGE firings, volunteers offer your crew some food and ask for help sorting abandoned service-desk stock. A rack holds uniforms for staff who aren’t coming back. It has more name badges than the welcome desk.
raw_milk.log_0: You haul stock until your shoulders and head ache. The ranger finds another uniform. It is immediately qualified to staff the empty desk.
raw_milk.log_1: You record the staffing account and laugh at the ranger’s coat-hanger demonstration. The hangers achieve perfect attendance while declining every visitor request.
raw_milk.choice_2: Take some food for the road
raw_milk.log_2: You take some food from the visitors’ donation. It’s the only queue today with somebody working at both ends.

tariff_whiplash.name: Lunch for the slogan
tariff_whiplash.desc: At a roadside tariff fair, an importer needs supplies for his public cost display. Across the aisle, a promoter offers your crew some food to repeat “China paid.” The importer has his American bank statement. The promoter has better sandwiches.
tariff_whiplash.choice_0: Donate supplies to the cost display
tariff_whiplash.log_0: You donate some supplies; the importer records your help. The American payment finally gets a display board as large as the foreign-payer slogan.
tariff_whiplash.choice_1: Take the food; repeat the slogan
tariff_whiplash.log_1: You collect some food and repeat the slogan. The importer corrects you with his payment record. The sandwich has purchased a very small spokesperson.
tariff_whiplash.choice_2: Use your paper; record the payment
tariff_whiplash.log_2: You use some supplies to document the actual payment. The importer points to his name. It has remained American throughout the promotion.

classic_civic_potluck.desc: At a pantry preparing for the 2025 SNAP cuts, volunteers welcome your hungry crew and any help you can spare. A senator’s tax-cut leaflet props up the short table leg. It’s finally supporting dinner.
classic_civic_potluck.log_0: You eat and take some food. The tax-cut leaflet stays under the table; removing it would cost everyone their lunch.
classic_civic_potluck.log_1: You record the volunteers and collect some food. They ask you to include the casserole before Washington counts it as unnecessary spending.
classic_civic_potluck.log_2: You donate some food. A volunteer tapes your receipt over the senator’s smile. The first thing on that leaflet that fed anyone.
classic_civic_potluck.name: Supporting dinner

classic_crossing_block_party.desc: Trump ordered steps toward closing the Education Department. At a PTA fundraiser, parents ask your stopped crew to feed the volunteers or record their mock clearance sale. A desk is labelled “POWER RETURNED TO PARENTS.” Two parents are arguing over how to lift it.
classic_crossing_block_party.choice_0: Share some food; join the sale
classic_crossing_block_party.log_0: You share some food and join the parents’ mock auction. The desk goes to whoever can explain long division without crying.
classic_crossing_block_party.log_1: You record the display for D.C. The chair marked “local control” still has a federal assembly diagram taped underneath.
classic_crossing_block_party.log_2: You leave some supplies and settle into the reading corner. The book opens without anyone first abolishing its publisher.
classic_crossing_block_party.name: Closing-time education

classic_freeway_mural.desc: After the DOGE park firings, neighbors are clearing a picnic shelter that maintenance staff used to handle. They wave your van over for help. A vine has reached the visitor-information window. It’s the first applicant willing to work for sunlight.
classic_freeway_mural.log_0: You drag branches until your shoulders ache. Everyone cheers when the picnic table emerges. It has survived its promotion to wilderness.
classic_freeway_mural.log_1: You donate some supplies; volunteers add your contribution to their account. The rake’s new handle makes it the park’s best-supported employee.
classic_freeway_mural.log_2: You record who did the maintenance before the firings. A squirrel interrupts. The volunteer refuses to list it as a contractor.
classic_freeway_mural.name: Unmanaged wilderness

classic_mail_drop.desc: At a library stop, volunteers give your crew letters about the nonexistent studies in the first MAHA report. They offer some food for an accurate recorded reply. A retired postman has brought an empty envelope. “That’s all the research we could fit.”
classic_mail_drop.log_0: You read and save the letters, laughing. The postman has underlined “address unknown” so hard the nonexistent study now has a window.
classic_mail_drop.log_1: You record the citation corrections and collect some food. The librarian checks the reply exists before pressing play.
classic_mail_drop.log_2: You share some food and sort the letters with the volunteers. Every missing study gets a real paperclip. The science budget is recovering.
classic_mail_drop.name: Return to nonexistent sender

classic_media_training.desc: At a health-funding teach-in, volunteers show your stopped crew how the 2025 Medicaid law changes eligibility and spending. They’ve built a demonstration ladder. The bottom rung is labelled “taxpayer.” The first reachable rung has been removed to keep the model affordable.
classic_media_training.name: The coverage ladder
classic_media_training.log_0: You check the sources and understand the changes. The volunteer restores the missing rung for packing. Even the demonstration needs it to work.
classic_media_training.log_1: You enjoy the rehearsal. The volunteer playing a senator praises the ladder from a stepladder somebody else brought.

classic_mutual_aid.desc: Trump’s tariffs have raised a tool co-op’s replacement bill. At your roadside stop, the owner offers $10 and some food for shifting repairable stock. Donated supplies would also help. A broken imported drill is being guarded by a perfectly American padlock.
classic_mutual_aid.log_0: You donate some supplies; the co-op records your contribution. The imported drill can finally be repaired using something cheaper than a patriotic speech.
classic_mutual_aid.log_1: You earn $10 and some food, sore but laughing. The owner locks the empty crate. “Still cheaper to insure than replace.”
classic_mutual_aid.log_2: You share some food and record the changed bills. The owner points to the lunch. “Our first import today without a surcharge.”
classic_mutual_aid.name: Imported freedom

classic_mutual_aid_dispatch.desc: Trump’s Gulf renaming has left a roadside map club with old charts and new federal labels. They ask your stopped crew to help prepare a public comparison. The volunteer has carefully checked the coast. It has made no effort to move.
classic_mutual_aid_dispatch.log_0: You donate some supplies and help document the labels. The volunteer uses a ruler to confirm that greatness added no coastline.
classic_mutual_aid_dispatch.choice_1: Share some food with the club
classic_mutual_aid_dispatch.log_1: You share some food, and everyone invents patriotic names for the crumbs. The plate becomes the first disputed territory to disappear.
classic_mutual_aid_dispatch.log_2: You compare and save the charts, relieved to find the coordinates unchanged. The volunteer gives the compass permission to remain neutral.
classic_mutual_aid_dispatch.name: Patriotic cartography

classic_neighborhood_watch.desc: After DOGE park staffing cuts, volunteers are making their own visitor guide. They wave your crew into the turnout and offer some food for hauling display boards. The official welcome mural has six smiling rangers. The actual ranger is asking the mural for directions.
classic_neighborhood_watch.name: Visitor disinformation
classic_neighborhood_watch.log_0: You document the volunteers’ guide and its sources. The ranger circles a working restroom. The mural’s career advice remains disappointing.
classic_neighborhood_watch.choice_1: Haul the boards for some food
classic_neighborhood_watch.log_1: You earn some food and a sore shoulder hauling boards. The painted rangers continue their excellent attendance record without lifting anything.
classic_neighborhood_watch.log_2: You laugh through the ranger’s tour. She introduces the painted staff individually. All six have apparently chosen to work remotely.

classic_overpass_stage.desc: At a roadside fair, residents protesting unlimited independent political spending ask your crew for testimony or help pushing their parade float. The float is a megaphone stuffed with imitation banknotes. It takes four people to make money talk.
classic_overpass_stage.log_0: You add your testimony to the residents’ record. The volunteer puts it beside the megaphone. Your voice has arrived without a forklift.
classic_overpass_stage.log_1: You push until your shoulders ache, laughing with the residents. The giant megaphone finally speaks: its wheel squeaks all the way downhill.
classic_overpass_stage.name: The people's megaphone

classic_press_briefing.desc: Your crew stops at a public briefing on the Trump administration’s proposed NIH overhead cap. A researcher has brought itemized costs, chairs, and an unplugged freezer to explain what “overhead” pays for. The demonstration ice is providing a floor-level impact assessment.
classic_press_briefing.name: The cost of the plug
classic_press_briefing.log_0: You verify the figures with a headache. The researcher adds electricity to the example. The ice has already submitted its objection.
classic_press_briefing.log_1: You sit and ease your sore legs. The researcher quietly plugs in a fan. Overhead immediately improves conditions for the taxpayer.
classic_press_briefing.log_2: You save the dated estimate and its proposal status. The researcher sets the papers above the puddle. That shelf is overhead too.

classic_press_pool_qna.desc: Your crew stops at a town museum’s public review, modelled on Trump’s Smithsonian history order. A board member wants an eviction photograph retitled “Family Relocation.” Former residents are waiting to speak. The family’s furniture is still visibly on the pavement.
classic_press_pool_qna.name: Approved memories
classic_press_pool_qna.log_0: You defend the dated account, head aching. The board member proposes cropping out the sofa. History is improving one cushion at a time.
classic_press_pool_qna.log_1: You stop arguing and repeat the caption. A former resident corrects you: people usually get to choose where they relocate the refrigerator.
classic_press_pool_qna.log_2: You rest outside and enjoy the quiet. Through the window, the board keeps moving the caption. The sofa hasn’t moved an inch.

classic_radio_phonebank.desc: A marina sign shop offers your stopped crew $8 to check labels following Trump’s federal Gulf renaming. The printer also welcomes witnesses to the old-and-new comparison. The label that says “America” costs more than the patch keeping the boat afloat.
classic_radio_phonebank.log_0: You learn the difference and laugh at the samples. The printer holds the old label over a leak. It remains impressively seaworthy.
classic_radio_phonebank.choice_1: Use your paper; record the changes
classic_radio_phonebank.log_1: You use some supplies to record the changes accurately. The marina’s coordinates fit on one line. Greatness requires a second sheet.
classic_radio_phonebank.log_2: You earn $8 and settle the spelling. The printer sticks the new name on a bucket. It still needs emptying.
classic_radio_phonebank.name: The eight-dollar gulf

classic_service_station.desc: Your hot, aching crew stops beside a travelling roofers’ protest against Florida’s ban on local heat mandates. Volunteers have shade and towels but need water. Their display shows a politician praising freedom from regulation beneath an umbrella held by somebody else.
classic_service_station.log_0: You use some water and recover in the shade. The volunteer wrings out a towel. Individual responsibility has soaked the bucket.
classic_service_station.log_1: You record the Florida rule and the roofers’ account. The display’s politician has a permanent parasol; everyone else has a shift rota.
classic_service_station.log_2: You leave some water for the workers. A roofer pours it into the cooler without first checking whether the county approved compassion.
classic_service_station.name: Break-room government

classic_union_blockade.desc: Residents at a roadside civic picnic are challenging unlimited super-PAC money with accounts from ordinary voters. They welcome your crew’s story and share food for the trip. A donor has lent a powerful loudspeaker. He keeps asking whether it can make him the electorate.
classic_union_blockade.choice_0: Add your account to the record
classic_union_blockade.log_0: You add your account and enjoy the residents’ applause. The donor tests the microphone. It still produces only one person.
classic_union_blockade.choice_1: Take some food for the road
classic_union_blockade.log_1: You collect some food. The cook gives everyone the same portion. The loudspeaker donor asks whether she has heard how loudly he contributes.
classic_union_blockade.choice_2: Share some food; join the picnic
classic_union_blockade.log_2: You share some food and enjoy the picnic. The donor’s speech competes with a crisp packet. The packet has better timing.
classic_union_blockade.name: One person, one microphone

classic_water_drive.desc: Trump’s tariffs have raised a community canner’s packaging bill. At your road stop, she asks for donated supplies or help shifting crates in exchange for some food. She holds up a tin. “This is the bit we’ve made too expensive to throw away.”
classic_water_drive.log_0: You donate some supplies, and she records your help. The soup can now reach people without needing its own investment prospectus.
classic_water_drive.log_1: You haul crates until your arms ache and earn some food. The canner asks you to bring back the tins before retiring on them.
classic_water_drive.name: The protected soup tin

deep_circuit_breaker.desc: A travelling trade fair celebrates Florida’s ban on local heat mandates with a “voluntary break” treadmill. Your hot crew stops beside it. The water cooler moves farther away whenever the belt turns. A roofer offers shade and asks for water donations.
deep_circuit_breaker.name: The freedom treadmill
deep_circuit_breaker.choice_0: Use some water; rest in shade
deep_circuit_breaker.log_0: You use some water and recover beside the roofer. The treadmill records your stationary body as a troubling decline in productivity.
deep_circuit_breaker.log_1: You stumble off with sore shins. The operator congratulates you on freely choosing to approach the cooler, which has reached the next county.
deep_circuit_breaker.choice_2: Donate some water; document the display
deep_circuit_breaker.log_2: You donate some water and document the display with the roofer. The cooler becomes accessible as soon as someone unplugs freedom.

deep_field_intel.desc: After the Pentagon accepted Qatar’s luxury jet, a roadside workers’ fair built a gift-inspection tunnel. Your crew is invited to compare it with their employer’s strict gift rule. A muffin cannot pass. The aircraft-shaped hole behind it is generously proportioned.
deep_field_intel.name: Gift capacity
deep_field_intel.choice_0: Use your paper; record the comparison
deep_field_intel.log_0: You use some supplies to save the jet report and workplace rule. The inspector measures the muffin again. Still dangerously low altitude.
deep_field_intel.choice_1: Donate supplies; help decorate the tunnel
deep_field_intel.log_1: You donate some supplies and enjoy decorating the tunnel. The muffin gets cardboard wings. The inspector suddenly requires a much smaller ruler.
deep_field_intel.choice_2: Watch from the quiet picnic table
deep_field_intel.log_2: You relax at the picnic table. The inspector walks around the aircraft-shaped hole searching for small gifts. The muffin remains under heavy guard.

deep_grassroots_signal.desc: A roadside technology fair recreates the Trump officials’ Signal scandal using sandwich plans. Your crew can inspect the recipient list. The demonstration journalist gets every detail. The person making lunch receives a message saying the schedule is too sensitive.
deep_grassroots_signal.name: The accidental recipient booth
deep_grassroots_signal.log_0: You verify the demonstration against the reported scandal. The sandwich maker finally gets the order by asking the journalist what’s for lunch.
deep_grassroots_signal.choice_1: Trace and save the message sequence
deep_grassroots_signal.log_1: You save the sequence with a headache. The operator adds another padlock to the lunch box. The message list remains wide open.
deep_grassroots_signal.choice_2: Post that nobody else saw it
deep_grassroots_signal.log_2: You post the wrong claim and get corrected. The demonstration journalist has already described the sandwich, its departure time, and the pickle.

deep_media_ambush.desc: Trump’s order to facilitate closing the Education Department has inspired a roadside “power returned to parents” booth. Your crew is handed an enormous demonstration parcel. Inside are unpaid tasks. The volunteer has helpfully attached a return label addressed to the parent holding it.
deep_media_ambush.name: Return to sender
deep_media_ambush.log_0: You document the proposal and question every task, head aching. The volunteer folds the return label into a circle. Local control is complete.
deep_media_ambush.log_1: You clear your head outside the demonstration. The parcel passes between parents. Nobody can find the end marked “empowerment.”
deep_media_ambush.choice_2: Announce the department is already abolished
deep_media_ambush.log_2: You enjoy a simpler story until a teacher corrects you: the closure directive wasn’t an act of Congress. Your parcel needs another label.

deep_memorandum_dump.desc: Trump’s tariffs have made a hardware importer’s invoice long enough to carpet his roadside shop. He invites your crew to inspect it. The charge paid by Americans runs past the till. The part where foreigners reimburse him is still awaiting delivery.
deep_memorandum_dump.name: The patriotic billfold
deep_memorandum_dump.choice_0: Check and save the invoice trail
deep_memorandum_dump.log_0: You save the verified bill, head aching from following it. The importer rolls up the reimbursement section. It’s the cardboard tube.
deep_memorandum_dump.choice_1: Use your paper; record the charges
deep_memorandum_dump.log_1: You use some supplies to document the charges accurately. The importer marks the American payer. You no longer need the entire floor plan.
deep_memorandum_dump.log_2: You clear your head outside. The importer closes the door carefully so it doesn’t pinch the part of the bill that bought the handle.

deep_state_dirge.desc: A fairground classroom inspired by Trump’s anti-indoctrination order admits questions only after they pass a patriotism test. Your crew stops at the gate. The test asks whether you agree with the test. A short exit slide is marked for people who already do.
deep_state_dirge.name: The unquestioning entrance
deep_state_dirge.choice_0: Use your paper; challenge the lesson
deep_state_dirge.log_0: You use some supplies documenting the proposal and arguing through the test until your head pounds. Your evidence gets detention for asking follow-ups.
deep_state_dirge.choice_1: Agree; take the quick exit slide
deep_state_dirge.log_1: You scrape an elbow on the slide and feel done with it. A teacher corrects your claim that patriotic approval proves historical accuracy.
deep_state_dirge.choice_2: Leave without taking the parents’ account
deep_state_dirge.log_2: You clear your head and leave without the parents’ evidence. The gate counts another visitor who has declined to question it.

deep_watch_party.desc: Your crew stops at a diner staging a version of Trump’s meme-coin investor dinner. The ordinary-voter table is behind three velvet ropes. The host offers to explain access. The cutlery has arrived by limousine; the people who wash it are still outside.
deep_watch_party.name: The ordinary-voter table
deep_watch_party.choice_0: Check the dinner report with workers
deep_watch_party.log_0: You verify the investor-access account, head aching. A dishwasher asks the host to introduce him as the person who holds all the forks.
deep_watch_party.log_1: You clear your head at the quiet counter. The host upgrades a spoon to the private room. It has excellent silver holdings.
deep_watch_party.log_2: You nap and miss the workers’ account. When you wake, the cutlery has finished its exclusive reception. The dishwashers are still waiting.

deep_watchdog_sync.desc: Your crew stops at a temp-work desk. The recruiter’s no-gifts briefing runs beneath a report about the Pentagon accepting Qatar’s jet. She seals a complimentary mint in an evidence bag. “Vendor influence.” The mint has achieved a level of scrutiny unavailable to most aircraft.
deep_watchdog_sync.name: The mint with foreign ties
deep_watchdog_sync.choice_0: Use your paper; record the comparison
deep_watchdog_sync.log_0: You use some supplies to save the workplace rule and jet report. The recruiter weighs the mint again. Its influence remains pocket-sized.
deep_watchdog_sync.log_1: You clear your head outside. Through the window, the recruiter is still completing the mint’s chain of custody.
deep_watchdog_sync.choice_2: Repeat that every gift is allowed
deep_watchdog_sync.log_2: You repeat the false blanket claim and get corrected. The recruiter points to the workplace rule. The mint remains detained pending lunch.

fundraiser_detour.desc: After DOGE park staff cuts, local volunteers have reopened a picnic area for the afternoon. Your crew is welcome to rest; donated supplies help them manage it. The visitor brochure calls the view priceless. The volunteer has priced the toilet paper separately.
fundraiser_detour.choice_0: Donate some supplies to the volunteers
fundraiser_detour.log_0: You donate some supplies, and the volunteers note your help. A roll goes straight to the restroom. The view remains completely unbothered.
fundraiser_detour.log_1: You rest and clear your head without using supplies. The volunteer turns the brochure face down. The actual view has better staffing.
fundraiser_detour.name: The unpaid view

town_hall_drift.desc: Parents invite your crew to a fourth-floor meeting about their board’s response to Trump’s anti-indoctrination order. The lift is broken. The proposed lesson teaches that complaining weakens the nation. The staircase offers several opportunities to test the curriculum.
town_hall_drift.name: The approved stairs
town_hall_drift.log_0: You climb and argue the sourced case, legs and head aching. The board asks for a more positive account of the stairs.
town_hall_drift.choice_1: Walk with parents to their picnic
town_hall_drift.log_1: You take the hilly route, legs sore but spirits lifted. A parent marks the broken lift absent. It receives full credit for patriotism.
town_hall_drift.log_2: You leave with a quieter head and no testimony to offer. The board’s attendance sheet has discovered another supporter of the current arrangement.

deep_waystation_boost.desc: Trump’s tariffs have a freight yard repeatedly relabelling the same imported stock. Your van reaches the queue as a pallet makes its third patriotic lap. A flagger offers a direct coned lane or an easier merge. The pallet has travelled farther than the job it’s bringing back.
deep_waystation_boost.log_0: You gain road and clear your head. The flagger gets you past the queue. The pallet begins another tour of American manufacturing.
deep_waystation_boost.log_1: You gain road through an easy merge. The crew enjoys seeing the same pallet return to the same worker, now wearing a different flag.
deep_waystation_boost.name: The returning jobs lane

deep_rustbelt_convoy.desc: After DOGE park staffing cuts, the remaining ranger is routing visitors around an unattended entrance. She offers your stopped crew a short open service lane if you share some water, or the signed public loop with her account. Her radio keeps asking an empty desk for assistance.
deep_rustbelt_convoy.choice_0: Share some water; take the short lane
deep_rustbelt_convoy.log_0: You share some water and gain road through the open lane. The ranger’s radio requests backup. She drinks it herself.
deep_rustbelt_convoy.choice_1: Take the public loop; record her account
deep_rustbelt_convoy.log_1: You gain road and record the staffing account. The empty desk has excellent radio discipline. It never interrupts anyone.
deep_rustbelt_convoy.name: The hydrated shortcut

deep_beltway_fastpass.desc: A surplus market copied Trump’s “Department of War” secondary title onto its gate. Defence points left; War points right. Both queues meet at the same exit. Your stopped crew gets a choice from the marshal: direct cones or a quieter merge. The gate is winning on both fronts.
deep_beltway_fastpass.name: Both ways to war
deep_beltway_fastpass.log_0: You gain road through the direct lane. Behind you, Defence and War continue negotiating access to the same broken gate hinge.
deep_beltway_fastpass.log_1: You gain road and clear your head in the quiet merge. The marshal removes a duplicate arrow. A naming dispute becomes one ordinary exit.

clinic_triage.desc: Your tired crew stops at a workshop preparing for Medicaid work checks due from 2027. A cleaner is filling in a practice form during her unpaid break. The form asks why she isn’t working. Volunteers offer a table for your own food and welcome help.
clinic_triage.name: A shift to prove the shift
clinic_triage.log_0: You read until your head aches. The cleaner lists her unpaid break as time spent explaining her unpaid break. The form requests detail.
clinic_triage.choice_1: Use some food; take a break
clinic_triage.log_1: You use some food and recover at the table. The cleaner turns the form face down. It cannot question chewing from that position.
clinic_triage.log_2: You donate some supplies, and volunteers add your help to their account. The cleaner finally gets a spare pen that doesn’t belong to another job.

overnight_briefing.desc: After Trump officials’ Signal scandal, a roadside freight desk has put its public rest-area directions through a privacy briefing. Your tired crew is welcome to wait. The dispatcher knows a quiet corner. The briefing presenter has accidentally sent the directions to the biscuit supplier.
overnight_briefing.name: The safe place to stop
overnight_briefing.log_0: You read until your head aches. The biscuit supplier knows where you can rest. The people operating the rest area await a secure reply.
overnight_briefing.log_1: You use some food and rest with a clearer head. The dispatcher closes the briefing window. The outdoor bench requires no recipient list.
overnight_briefing.choice_2: Ask the dispatcher about the quiet corner
overnight_briefing.log_2: The dispatcher becomes a local contact and shows you a place to rest. She writes her number down without adding a journalist.

sat_straw_reserve.name: The adhesive boom
sat_straw_reserve.desc: At a grocery hit by Trump’s tariffs, your crew can buy some food for $6 or earn $10 applying revised prices. The owner has run out of shelf space for the stickers. American manufacturing has begun with a very large order of glue.
sat_straw_reserve.log_0: You pay $6 and collect some food. The cashier peels off the old price. It comes away more reluctantly than the patriotic flag.
sat_straw_reserve.log_1: You earn $10 and a headache. By closing time, the shelf is mostly adhesive. The promised manufacturing boom has reached your thumb.
sat_straw_reserve.log_2: You pass and leave dispirited. The affordability display has put its own prices out of reach.

sat_corn_bullets.name: Actual-size science
sat_corn_bullets.desc: A library fair is checking the nonexistent studies from the initial MAHA report. The organizer offers your crew $8 to correct the display cards. The original author table has empty chairs. The corrected version needs actual people, which is proving a serious catering complication.
sat_corn_bullets.choice_0: Check and save the citation history
sat_corn_bullets.log_0: You save the original and corrected references with a headache. The organizer cancels the imaginary seating plan. The room becomes smaller and more accurate.
sat_corn_bullets.log_1: You earn $8 and enjoy crossing out the fictional study. It is the first government-inspired job here completed without needing an imaginary qualification.
sat_corn_bullets.log_2: You leave dispirited. The empty author chair has acquired a ribbon. The organizer still needs somebody who exists to move it.

sat_grant_groceries.name: The desk survived
sat_grant_groceries.desc: After DOGE park firings, a campground association is moving the unused service desk into its volunteer tent. They offer your crew $12 for lifting, or welcome supplies. The coordinator calls the desk “excess bureaucracy.” It still has to go somewhere people can ask for toilet paper.
sat_grant_groceries.log_0: You donate some supplies and gain a local contact. The coordinator finds your details easily; the desk’s staff directory has plenty of space.
sat_grant_groceries.log_1: You earn $12 with aching arms. The coordinator empties the drawer of unused name badges. Smaller government becomes surprisingly easier to lift.
sat_grant_groceries.log_2: You leave dispirited. The empty service desk remains outside the volunteer tent, continuing its successful transition out of public service.

sat_cow_citations.name: The foldout electorate
sat_cow_citations.desc: A roadside café hosts a bookkeeper’s public guide to unlimited super-PAC money; some food costs $5. Your crew stops beside a sample donor ledger. The ordinary voter fits on a receipt. The billionaire requires a foldout that has reached the next table.
sat_cow_citations.choice_0: Check and save the spending rules
sat_cow_citations.log_0: You save the checked rules and examples, head aching. The bookkeeper folds the billionaire away. Several ordinary voters become visible underneath.
sat_cow_citations.log_1: You pay $5 and collect some food. The cook gives your order equal time on the grill. The ledger’s largest donor has not been consulted.
sat_cow_citations.log_2: You leave dispirited. The bookkeeper opens another foldout. The electorate is going to need a larger tablecloth.

sat_forecast_corrected.name: Patriotically air-conditioned
sat_forecast_corrected.desc: Florida barred local heat-break rules. At a roadside trade fair, a contractor wants the same freedom here. He praises toughness from inside a refrigerated sales trailer. A worker points you toward shade; the trailer’s exhaust is blowing directly onto her.
sat_forecast_corrected.log_0: Food and shade restore you. The contractor shuts his trailer window to explain more comfortably why workers need fewer protections.
sat_forecast_corrected.log_1: His certainty calms you. You repeat it; the worker offers to swap places with his air conditioner. Your authority evaporates.
sat_forecast_corrected.log_2: You leave irritated. The contractor puts on a cardigan before recording another message about people becoming too sensitive to heat.

sat_parking_gulf.name: The drain is unpatriotic
sat_parking_gulf.desc: Trump ordered “Gulf of America” onto federal maps. At a flooded parking stop, the owner offers $7 to repaint his sign. The attendant asks for a drain. He hands her a flag.
sat_parking_gulf.log_0: Seven dollars and a headache. The owner salutes the new gulf while you wring the old water out of your socks.
sat_parking_gulf.log_1: Drivers trust your arrow. The attendant asks whether draining an American gulf now counts as surrendering territory.
sat_parking_gulf.log_2: You leave disappointed. His flag falls into the puddle. He blames Mexico.

sat_library_minimum.name: The raccoon has seniority
sat_library_minimum.desc: After DOGE’s park-staff cuts, you stop at a park-side shop. The clerk offers $9 to fold trail leaflets. Outside, a bin overflows beneath AMERICA THE BEAUTIFUL. A raccoon is wearing somebody’s entire picnic.
sat_library_minimum.log_0: You share food and exchange numbers, enjoying a laugh. She locks the door before the raccoon applies for management.
sat_library_minimum.log_1: Nine dollars and aching eyes. The clerk endorses your careful folding. Washington’s savings now require the gift shop’s wages.
sat_library_minimum.log_2: You leave disappointed. The raccoon climbs onto the information desk, becoming the first park employee to receive lunch.

sat_tariff_forklift.name: America First, bend from the knees
sat_tariff_forklift.desc: Trump acknowledged deportations were taking workers from farms and hotels. At a produce yard, a manager offers $14 to move crates or food for sorting labels. His DEPORT THEM ALL sticker remains on the forklift. He has taped HELP WANTED underneath.
sat_tariff_forklift.log_0: Fourteen dollars and a sore back. The manager asks if you know anyone else, briefly expanding his preferred immigration policy to bring friends.
sat_tariff_forklift.log_1: You earn supplies and a headache. The manager keeps searching the help-wanted responses for somebody his bumper sticker has not already fired.
sat_tariff_forklift.log_2: You leave without earnings. The manager turns the forklift around so its political position stops addressing the hiring queue.

sat_alternator_tariff.name: China’s card declined
sat_alternator_tariff.desc: Trump says China pays the tariffs. At a roadside shop, your supplies cost $12. The cashier taps a Chinese flag against the card reader. Declined.
sat_alternator_tariff.log_0: Your payment works. “Congratulations,” she says. “You’re China now.”
sat_alternator_tariff.log_1: She circles the tariff. “China’s very generous with your money.”
sat_alternator_tariff.log_2: You leave empty-handed. The tariff has successfully protected the supplies from Americans.

sat_billion_pothole.name: A donation you can trip over
sat_billion_pothole.desc: Super PACs accept unlimited contributions. You stop at an event depot offering $10 to carry a donor’s giant ceremonial cheque. Its accompanying poster says every citizen has a voice. The cheque is too wide to fit through the citizens’ entrance.
sat_billion_pothole.choice_0: Save the terms and donor display
sat_billion_pothole.log_0: You document the arrangement, head aching. The donor’s speech is officially independent; it still requires three people and a loading door.
sat_billion_pothole.log_1: Ten dollars and sore muscles. The donor signs in one effortless stroke; you need to sit down after delivering his free speech.
sat_billion_pothole.log_2: You leave disappointed. A worker removes the public entrance sign so the donor’s equal voice can scrape through sideways.

sat_bridge_bullets.name: Working on proof of working
sat_bridge_bullets.desc: Congress added Medicaid work requirements for 2027. At a community information table, a cleaner practices assembling proof of shifts between shifts. The sample form asks why she missed the workshop. Her payslip is still damp from the job that prevented her attending.
sat_bridge_bullets.log_0: You document the mismatch, mentally drained. The cleaner’s work prevented her proving she works. The sample answer box is admirably small.
sat_bridge_bullets.log_1: You share food and exchange numbers. She eats while sorting payslips, providing evidence that employment can interfere with both lunch and paperwork.
sat_bridge_bullets.log_2: You leave frustrated. She asks whether attending a workshop about proving work can itself count as work. Nobody has brought that form.

sat_press_pool_radio.name: Cabinet-level contact management
sat_press_pool_radio.desc: Trump’s team included a journalist in its Signal strike chat. At a café showing the news, the owner offers $8 to clear a tour bus’s tables. The cashier needs his PIN to refund mayonnaise.
sat_press_pool_radio.log_0: You confirm the report. The café’s new security procedure is asking who the people in the chat actually are.
sat_press_pool_radio.log_1: Eight dollars and a headache. You match forgotten phones to passengers. The café’s standards now exceed national security’s.
sat_press_pool_radio.log_2: You leave unpaid. The mayonnaise refund remains behind a stronger security procedure than the airstrikes.

sat_hydration_pressure.name: Freedom reaches the tuna
sat_hydration_pressure.desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation. At a truck stop, a celebratory display sprays the sandwich counter. The clerk offers $9 to brace it. Ordinary showers are free if you bring soap. The tuna has already exercised its freedom.
sat_hydration_pressure.choice_0: Use your soap; take a shower
sat_hydration_pressure.log_0: Clean at last. On your way out, a tuna sandwich makes a determined break for the drain.
sat_hydration_pressure.log_1: Nine dollars and aching arms. You hold freedom upright while the clerk evacuates the egg mayonnaise.
sat_hydration_pressure.log_2: You leave unwashed. The display has liberated half the lunch menu; the remaining sandwiches are gathering on higher ground.

sat_museum_grant.name: Education, some assembly required
sat_museum_grant.desc: Trump directed the Education Department’s closure as far as law permits. At a school fundraiser, an organizer offers $11 to sort donated books. A volunteer is using the closure flyer to prop up a broken shelf. Finally, the policy is supporting education.
sat_museum_grant.log_0: Eleven dollars and aching eyes. You shelve the books; the closure flyer holds steady in its first successful teaching-support role.
sat_museum_grant.log_1: You share lunch and a laugh. She adds another closure flyer beneath the shelf, strengthening education through repeated calls to dismantle it.
sat_museum_grant.log_2: You leave disappointed. The shelf needs more support; the volunteer asks whether Washington has printed anything else about providing less.

sat_factcheck_shift.name: Gold-standard stapling
sat_factcheck_shift.desc: The MAHA report cited nonexistent studies. A copy shop offers $15 to collate report booklets for a public discussion. The printer says missing pages are your fault, but missing science is apparently a formatting issue. He checks your staples more carefully than the references.
sat_factcheck_shift.log_0: Fifteen dollars, evidence, and a headache. Every page is now attached to something real, which puts the staples ahead of several citations.
sat_factcheck_shift.log_1: Your grand reading gets a laugh. You endorse a nonexistent paper; the printer asks whether your application to the commission is pending.
sat_factcheck_shift.log_2: You leave disappointed. The printer checks another staple, still the only part of the report willing to hold under light pressure.

sat_food_shelf.name: Federal savings, local shoulders
sat_food_shelf.desc: USDA cancelled local-food purchasing funds. At a co-op loading bay, an organizer offers food for packing donated groceries or $10 for sorting delivery slips. The cancelled order is easy to lift. Everything replacing it is in crates.
sat_food_shelf.log_0: You earn supplies and a sore back. The federal savings arrive in your shoulders, considerably heavier than they looked in the announcement.
sat_food_shelf.log_1: Ten dollars and a headache. Each address gets matched to food; Washington’s contribution remains a remarkably lightweight cancellation notice.
sat_food_shelf.log_2: You leave without earnings. The organizer folds the cancellation into a tiny square. Unfortunately, the crates refuse to become equally efficient.

sat_cabinet_guest.name: The sea forgot its new name
sat_cabinet_guest.desc: Trump ordered federal maps to say Gulf of America. At a marine-supply counter, a customer demands an American refund because his old chart still says Mexico. The clerk has the order. The customer checks his shoes for foreign seawater.
sat_cabinet_guest.log_0: You save the actual naming change, head aching. The clerk explains that the water did not relocate; the customer looks personally betrayed by geography.
sat_cabinet_guest.log_1: The crew laughs until you invent a maritime border change. The clerk takes the chart away before your geography reaches the fish.
sat_cabinet_guest.log_2: You leave irritated. The customer wrings out a sock and asks whether the shop can exchange the water for the patriotic version.

sat_name_infrastructure.name: The map has already won
sat_name_infrastructure.desc: Albuquerque reported a federal attempt to withdraw its Rail Trail grant. At a Beltway transport-book stall, a $6 route print still shows the promised path. The clerk keeps the withdrawal notice beside it. The funding has become harder to locate than the destination.
sat_name_infrastructure.log_0: You keep the six-dollar print as evidence. A dotted line remains the cheapest way to deliver infrastructure without anyone having to walk on it.
sat_name_infrastructure.choice_1: Compare the notice with the map
sat_name_infrastructure.log_1: You save a careful comparison, head aching. The clerk draws the uncertain funding in pencil, finally giving the path an accurate surface.
sat_name_infrastructure.log_2: You leave disappointed. The print reaches the destination beautifully; the people who might use the actual path have received a notice instead.

sat_straw_inspection.name: Small government inspects your straw
sat_straw_inspection.desc: Trump ordered federal agencies to stop using paper straws. At a burger stand, the owner films inspections of customers’ drinks as his own patriotic tribute. The cashier points out that customers are not federal agencies. He asks her to stop weakening the border.
sat_straw_inspection.log_0: You share food and confirm her point. She eats while he carefully investigates whether the burger wrapper is conspiring with the straw.
sat_straw_inspection.choice_1: Read and save the actual order
sat_straw_inspection.log_1: You save the order through a headache. His federal jurisdiction shrinks until it no longer reaches the milkshake currently in front of him.
sat_straw_inspection.log_2: You leave irritated. He demands another close-up of the straw, which has now received more oversight than the owner’s payroll.

sat_shower_force.name: The shower has taken the hair
sat_shower_force.desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation after years of complaining about water pressure. At a hardware launch, the demonstration blasts the wig off a presidential mannequin. The clerk offers $12 to mop; ordinary traveler showers cost $5. The wig is heading for plumbing reform.
sat_shower_force.log_0: Twelve dollars and a sore back. You catch the wig on the mop, briefly becoming the best-groomed cleaner in the building.
sat_shower_force.log_1: Five dollars buys a proper wash. The ordinary shower leaves your hair attached, an achievement the demonstration has chosen not to emphasize.
sat_shower_force.log_2: You leave disappointed. The clerk puts the wet wig back on the mannequin, which now looks less certain about freedom.

sat_receipt_museum.name: Same bombs, new letterhead
sat_receipt_museum.desc: Trump gave the Defense Department “Department of War” as a second name. At a print shop, the printer offers $13 to sort new letterheads. He presents two invoices. “Same bombs. Twice the stationery.”
sat_receipt_museum.log_0: You sort both names, save the invoices, and earn $13, head aching. The printer needs another cabinet for the expanded letterhead supply.
sat_receipt_museum.log_1: You announce two armies by mistake. The crew laughs; the printer doubles his quote. You both briefly understand government contracting.
sat_receipt_museum.log_2: You leave unpaid. The printer asks whether peace needs a separate invoice or whether nobody is ordering that.

sat_transit_ribbon.name: The trail has become a notice
sat_transit_ribbon.desc: Albuquerque reported a federal attempt to withdraw Rail Trail money. At a Beltway supporters’ stall, the printer offers $9 to fold leaflets. A volunteer’s bicycle leans against the funding announcement. It is the only transport here receiving actual support from the paperwork.
sat_transit_ribbon.log_0: You share food and gain a contact. She moves the leaflet stack under her bicycle’s wobbly stand, getting one useful public service from it.
sat_transit_ribbon.log_1: Nine dollars and aching eyes earn an endorsement. You make the withdrawal notice compact enough for people to carry while walking.
sat_transit_ribbon.log_2: You leave disappointed. The volunteer rings her bicycle bell; the funding notice remains considerably less capable of moving people.

sat_weather_desk.name: The park is open in the photograph
sat_weather_desk.desc: DOGE cut national-park staff. At a park-side concession, the owner offers $6 to hang a FULL SERVICE banner over a closed information window. A worker has the staffing notices. The owner says the photograph needs somebody helpful, preferably somebody not asking for wages.
sat_weather_desk.log_0: You document the mismatch, head aching. The helpful employee in the publicity photograph has become a cheaper substitute for someone who can answer questions.
sat_weather_desk.log_1: You earn $6 and lose trust. A visitor asks the closed window for directions; the banner provides an excellent view of its own confidence.
sat_weather_desk.log_2: You leave unpaid and annoyed. The owner places a cardboard ranger behind the glass. Its first shift goes exactly as well as expected.

sat_bibliography_emergency.name: The bandage exists
sat_bibliography_emergency.desc: The MAHA report cited nonexistent studies. At a community health fair, a printer offers $12 to collate discussion leaflets. A nurse can treat you with your supplies. Her bandages have an unfair scientific advantage: she can point to where they are.
sat_bibliography_emergency.log_0: You save the error list, earn $12, and acquire a headache. Every leaflet is physically present; several things it cites remain more ambitious.
sat_bibliography_emergency.log_1: The nurse uses your supplies and patches you up. One verified source, applied directly.
sat_bibliography_emergency.log_2: You leave disappointed. The nurse opens another real bandage beside the report’s much more imaginative approach to supporting a claim.

west_grant_translation.name: The grant wants a flag
west_grant_translation.desc: Trump’s patriotic-education order reaches a school-display printer. The printer offers $12 to sort revised classroom captions. A teacher shows you the old and proposed versions: the discussion question has been replaced by a flag large enough to prevent further questions.
west_grant_translation.log_0: You earn $12 and a headache. The flag fits perfectly over the space where a student might previously have developed an opinion.
west_grant_translation.log_1: You preserve the difference, mentally tired. The proposed lesson has one fewer question and a much more confident answer supplied in advance.
west_grant_translation.log_2: You leave the offer behind. The teacher measures the remaining discussion space, which is now chiefly the gap beneath the flagpole.

west_rail_replacement.name: The campaign for a path needs a van
west_rail_replacement.desc: Albuquerque reported an attempted federal withdrawal of Rail Trail funds. At a coastal transport meeting, an organizer offers $15 to deliver campaign materials using your own packing supplies. A commuter has the correspondence. Once again, the working route belongs to somebody else.
west_rail_replacement.log_0: You spend supplies and earn $15. The posters promising movement reach the meeting because the van never waited for the funding announcement.
west_rail_replacement.choice_1: Compare the correspondence with the commuter
west_rail_replacement.log_1: You gain evidence and a contact, head aching. The promised path currently moves most efficiently when printed small enough for somebody to carry.
west_rail_replacement.log_2: You leave the offer behind. The organizer checks your van’s departure time with more urgency than the campaign’s map has ever received.

west_laboratory_overhead.name: Science would like a room
west_laboratory_overhead.desc: Trump’s NIH overhead-cap proposal put research facilities’ running costs at risk. At a laboratory open day, $14 is offered for sorting equipment tags. A nurse offers basic care using shared supplies. The funding display celebrates experiments while treating their building as a suspicious luxury.
west_laboratory_overhead.choice_0: Sort tags; save the budget comparison
west_laboratory_overhead.log_0: Fourteen dollars earned; your eyes ache. The refrigerator’s tag identifies an essential instrument, despite its scandalous habit of needing electricity.
west_laboratory_overhead.log_1: You recover and gain a contact. The nurse uses an actual room, quietly committing several of the proposal’s less glamorous expenses.
west_laboratory_overhead.log_2: You leave the offer behind. A researcher closes the door so the experiment can continue benefiting from the controversial invention of indoors.

west_wind_loyalty.name: The wind has not read the order
west_wind_loyalty.desc: Trump paused new federal wind-project approvals. At a turbine-repair stall, a technician offers $10 to sort spare-part labels. He keeps the order under a paperweight. The breeze removes the paperweight’s supporting documents every time somebody praises the pause.
west_wind_loyalty.log_0: Ten dollars and a headache. The technician retrieves another page from the hedge; wind continues producing results without waiting for the speech to finish.
west_wind_loyalty.log_1: You gain evidence and a contact, mentally tired. He distinguishes paused approvals from moving air, a distinction the flying order demonstrates repeatedly.
west_wind_loyalty.log_2: You leave the offer behind. A speaker asks someone to hold the paperwork still while he explains the advantages of stopping wind development.

west_desert_pressure.name: The tank has run out of freedom
west_desert_pressure.desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation. At a desert service stop, a celebratory display is draining the tank. The plumber offers water for help shutting it off or $12 for the heavier work. The owner asks whether the empty tank is refusing to cooperate politically.
west_desert_pressure.choice_0: Help shut it off; take water
west_desert_pressure.log_0: You gain water and some peace of mind. The plumber demonstrates the off switch, a technology omitted from the freedom ceremony.
west_desert_pressure.log_1: Twelve dollars and sore muscles. You haul the equipment while the owner asks whether refilling the tank counts as government interference.
west_desert_pressure.log_2: You leave the offer behind. The display coughs; the owner checks the banner instead of the water level.

west_beef_passports.name: The flag is not a customs form
west_beef_passports.desc: Trump says tariffs make foreigners pay. At a wholesale depot, $16 is offered to sort shipment labels. The owner puts American flags over imported-stock markings. The dispatcher has the original invoices. The flags have shown no interest in paying the tariff either.
west_beef_passports.log_0: Sixteen dollars and a headache. Every flag is removed long enough for the box’s actual origin to become inconvenient again.
west_beef_passports.log_1: You save the contradiction through aching eyes. The tariff arrived in dollars payable here, despite the owner’s best efforts to give it a foreign address.
west_beef_passports.log_2: You leave the work behind. The owner adds a larger flag, increasing the box’s patriotism without reducing its bill.

play.travel_help: Set your pace and information diet, then travel. The road runs briefly before stopping at your next decision. Watch the gauges; choices and repairs report their actual costs.
play.outfit_help: Your starting funds pay for the selected cart. There are no free supplies underneath it. Add or remove food, water, parts and protection; you may leave empty. Purchases are charged when you depart. A spare is consumed only when fitted.
play.resupply_help: Choose supplies, parts and protection, then review the total. Buying charges your cash immediately and returns you to town. Leaving the store does not charge you. A spare is consumed only when fitted.
play.review_help: Check what you are carrying and what you will have left. These purchases happen when you start the journey.
play.capacity: Supplies are capped at 20. Extra provisions above that limit do not carry over.
play.pack_empty: A starter load is selected. Every item comes out of your funds—change or remove anything.
play.fuel_food_help: Food and water add supplies. Water also gives you a water-jug equipment tag.
play.vehicle_help: One matching spare is consumed when fitted. Without one, repairs may cost cash, time, or vehicle condition.
play.ppe_help: Protective gear softens specific weather penalties. Select an item to see what it protects against.
play.docs_help: A press pass can help at permit checks. A legal fund adds credibility.
play.pace_help: Steady adds no pace fatigue. Heated costs 1 Sanity and Blitz costs 2 per 5 hours of driving; unfinished fatigue carries into later drives. Weather and vehicle condition affect distance, and activities use available driving time.
play.diet_help: Your information diet is your news intake. Its Sanity effect applies once per day. Quieter coverage supports Sanity; doomscrolling improves your chances of finding receipts but costs Sanity.
play.locked: Today’s settings are locked until the next day.
play.weather_help: These modifiers describe the current weather. Conditions can change as the next day begins. Protective gear can replace some penalties.
play.cred_help: Credibility rises by listening to locals, documenting events and useful encounter choices. Misleading claims and some shortcuts reduce it. It affects the final hearing.
play.morale_help: Morale is the crew’s shared spirit. Care, rest, cooperation and successful encounters raise it. Losses, departures, hunger and difficult choices lower it.
play.sanity_help: News intake, rushed travel, illness and stressful choices can lower sanity. Quiet news, camp recovery and helpful encounters restore it. A warning appears at 2 or less.
play.health_help: Health falls through injury, hunger and hard physical work. Care, recovery days and some encounters restore it. At zero the journey ends.
play.supplies_help: Food and water share a 20-unit capacity. Travel, weather, care and barter use supplies. Buy provisions, gather outside town, trade or work for food to replenish them.
play.allies_help: Allies are outside supporters, separate from the people in your van. Helpful encounter choices build support; choices that spend or alienate support reduce it. Allies contribute to the final hearing.
play.travel_wait: Watch the road. Your next decision is approaching.
play.travel_done: You made it through this stretch.
play.journal_empty: The journal fills as your journey unfolds.
play.repair_help: Choose a repair and review its cost before fitting a part or calling for help.
play.danger: Sanity is in the danger zone
play.danger_help: Your sanity is 2 or lower. Consider rest or a quieter information diet before pushing on.
play.unknown_log: Trail conditions changed. Check the latest resource receipt.
play.seed_hint: Use a run code to replay a journey. Leave the generated code as-is for this trip.
play.receipts_help: 证据是带到D.C.听证会的资料。选择标有“证据 +1”的遭遇选项即可获得。每份保留的证据为旅程得分增加8分。只有明确标注消耗证据的选项才会减少数量。

ACT-BARTERTIRE.setup: At the community exchange, a resident offers a tire for supplies. A nearby radio discusses unlimited political spending. You check whether the tire comes with a senator.
ACT-BARTERTIRE.outcome: The tire is yours. No senator included, but it may actually get you somewhere.

ACT-CASHWORK.title: Family Values Payroll
ACT-CASHWORK.setup: A diner offers $18 for a three-hour cleanup. The owner praises Trump’s “no tax on tips” promise. You ask about the wage. He points at the tip jar.
ACT-CASHWORK.outcome: You collect the $18 and lose some patience. The empty tip jar enjoys a completely tax-free afternoon.

ACT-FOODWORK.title: Your Dinner, Your Assignment
ACT-FOODWORK.setup: A pantry offers food for a three-hour sorting shift. Congress has cut projected food-aid spending. The volunteer calls your crate “the local implementation plan.”
ACT-FOODWORK.outcome: You finish tired and take the food. Congress can call it self-sufficiency; you have seen the donation labels.

ACT-FORAGE.title: No Payslip Required
ACT-FORAGE.setup: A local guide leads a foraging walk while neighbors discuss Congress’s food-aid work rules. The blackberry bush has failed to install a document-upload portal.
ACT-FORAGE.outcome: You gather some food. The bush accepts evidence that you are hungry. Washington may want to audit it.

ACT-GLEAN.title: The Tariff Harvest
ACT-GLEAN.setup: A farmer lets your crew glean produce while grumbling about tariffs on tractor parts. His crops grew locally. Their operating expenses have been around the world.
ACT-GLEAN.outcome: You work the row and collect food, sore from the effort. The farmer waves a repair bill. “China missed another payment.”

ACT-REST.title: Restoration of Executive Function
ACT-REST.setup: The crew can rest for a day. After another DOGE efficiency story, someone suggests firing the tired people. This would leave the van impressively understaffed.
ACT-REST.outcome: Rest restores what it can. You retain the staff, including the person who knows where the keys are.

CARE-06.continuing: {name} is exhausted from the tariff dispute. China has not sent a relief driver.
CARE-06.critical: {name} is critically unwell. Pressing on without care now will kill them. If this is your character, the journey will end.

CARE-08.continuing: {name} remains injured. The donor’s speech about self-reliance has required another pair of hands to turn the pages.
